analysis:
Only documentation changed (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md and docs/architecture/inference.md); no executable source was supplied. The new inference.md Context text (head lines ~25-171) describes the unregistered NemotronSuperLocalBridgeBuilder, NemotronSuperLocalLoad, NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP (authenticated local hook, absent by default, 429 on queueFull, 'No production caller installs it'), env-controlled concurrency, MTP opt-in (DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP=1), image ingest (PNG/JPEG only, charged before decode) and an exact-prefix checkpoint-bank cache. The doc states these paths register no model and expose no public route or coordinator path, so the supplied evidence shows no regression to TB-002/TB-007/TB-011 gating and no change to A-001 exposure.

Items for a later pass if code lands or is wired into production:
(1) T-041/SEC-035: the doc says Super text requests use a 'local unscoped cache scope' with resident prefix reuse when DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1. T-041 says production creates no resident-RAM prefix cache and that cacheSalt is coordinator-authored. This is only safe while the owner is unregistered or local-only; if it is ever reachable via coordinator traffic, the cross-tenant TTFT oracle and the T-041 scoping and mitigation text would need updating. The threat model currently has no entry for this local-only resident cache.
(2) The local HTTP hook (authenticated app, image/JSON/base64 parsing, ingress and media charges) is new attack surface if installed. It needs verification of authentication and bounds in NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP and NemotronSuperLocalBridgeBuilder; those files were not supplied.
(3) Resident checkpoint bank and prefill-lane memory reservations, held until native retirement, and the speculation 256 MiB unmeasured scratch allowance bear on T-010/T-029 DoS and T-028 residual data.
(4) The inference.md line ~890 change points to a shared media discovery policy in model-registry.md, which was not supplied.
The doc claims are unverified by code in this batch. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
